intro.title: Undo/Redo
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple text editor that allows you to undo and redo your changes. You will learn how to manage application state by storing a history of user actions. The core programming concept is the Command Pattern, which you'll implement using arrays to track past and future states. You'll use Angular components, TypeScript arrays, and event handling to create this feature. By the end, you'll have a working editor where you can type text and navigate through your edit history with undo and redo buttons.
intro.usecase: The undo/redo pattern is essential in any interactive application where users need to correct mistakes or explore different states without fear of permanent errors. You'll see this in text editors like Google Docs, where users can revert formatting changes, in design tools like Figma for adjusting element properties, and in complex form-based dashboards where administrators might modify multiple data filters or settings. As an Angular developer, implementing this pattern allows you to build more professional, user-friendly interfaces that handle state changes predictably and safely.
